Humanoids

Atlas gains a four-finger hand with 13 degrees of freedom

Boston Dynamics trades a little finger for more articulated control, tactile sensing and simulation-based training.

The Robot Report ↗1 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

More articulation in four fingers

Boston Dynamics has presented an Atlas hand with four fingers and 13 degrees of freedom, up from seven in the previous design. The thumb has four degrees of freedom and the other fingers have three each. Removing the little finger reduces size, power demand and complexity while targeting a large human-hand form factor.

Actuation and contact sensing

Direct joint actuation uses a common actuator type without transmission cables crossing joints. Pressure sensors in the fingertips and palm complement joint feedback to detect contact and slipping. Demonstrations include picking, reorienting objects within the hand and operating tool triggers, capabilities that matter when a robot handles equipment built for people.

Learning before deployment

Reinforcement learning in simulation varies torque, friction and geometry to help transfer control to real hardware. The announcement concerns an improved hand and its control approach. It does not provide standardized task success rates or long-term service-life evidence demonstrating readiness for every industrial job.
